entry.title: [BIP Proposal] Anti-Fee-Sniping with LockTime
entry.summary:
The utilization of nLockTime in Bitcoin Core and Electrum, which has been a part of these systems since 2014 and 2017 respectively, integrates an anti-fee-sniping feature that is now being formalized through BIP326. This new proposal delineates the use of nSequence for certain taproot transactions instead of relying solely on nLockTime, marking a significant shift in approach within the protocol's operations.
The draft of the new BIP, accessible at [this GitHub repository](https://github.com/nervana21/bips/blob/anti-fee-snipe/bip-anti-fee-sniping-with-locktime.md), closely adheres to existing functions like DiscourageFeeSniping and IsCurrentForAntiFeeSniping from Bitcoin Core's codebase. It specifies setting nLockTime to the current blockchain tip height, with a 10% chance of subtracting a random integer up to 0.99 from this value, subsequently clamping the result at zero to prevent negative values. Notably, nLockTime cannot be reset if it matches the tip height or is set during the initial block download phase, or if the tip's age exceeds eight hours, ensuring stability and consistency in transaction processing.
Additionally, the policy refrains from modifying nLockTime if it has been pre-set or if any transaction input already possesses a defined nSequence, maintaining integrity across different transaction scenarios. The inclusion of test vectors in the BIP draft aims to facilitate understanding and implementation by developers, promoting robust feedback and iterative improvements. This initiative underscores a focused effort to enhance transaction privacy and efficiency through nuanced technical adjustments in the Bitcoin ecosystem.
